one_month_reasoning: Several industry events fall inside the window. Samsung's Q3 preliminary results come around 7-8 Oct. Korea's 1-20 Oct exports come around 21 Oct (September chip exports were +263% y/y). SK hynix reports Q3 on about 27 Oct, and Samsung's full Q3 and Kioxia's results land around 29-30 Oct. Hyperscaler results in late October, including 2027 capex commentary, also fall here. TrendForce's 4Q26 contract data (+10-15% conventional DRAM, HBM 2027 ASP +121%) means peer prints are likely to confirm tight supply, so the fundamental news flow should lean positive. But MU's own large beat-and-raise (FQ1 guide about 8% above consensus) moved the stock only +0.9% net in two sessions, so good news looks largely priced. The risk to watch is a 'second-derivative' story: slowing price increases and any capex digestion talk from hyperscalers. I take a slight positive drift for post-earnings-surprise momentum (median $1,085) and a lognormal sigma of 20%, a little under 80%/3.5 because the earnings event has passed.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (FY28-ish EPS $195 x 5.5x = $1,073, 45%), EV/EBITDA ($245B x 3.5x + ~$160B net cash over 1.15B shares = $885, 25%) and normalized mid-cycle ($95 x 12x + $60 net cash = $1,200, 30%), giving about $1,064, close to the current price.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY28 $205.95 haircut ~5% because TrendForce says increases are moderating (conventional DRAM +10-15% QoQ in 4Q26 vs bigger prior gains) and BofA models a ~5% 2028 DRAM ASP retreat from the 2027 peak.

Memory-maker peer fwd P/E 3.97-8.04x (median ~4.5x); full 11-peer median 4.92x. MU trades at 6.09x today. 5.5x keeps MU inside the memory range, a modest premium to Korean/Taiwan peers for US listing and the SCA floor-price RPO (~$150B), but below today's 6.1x because by Oct-2027 the market will be looking at 2028 supply additions.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY28 EBITDA ~$245B x 3.5x = $858B EV + ~$160B projected net cash, / 1.15B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: FQ4 non-GAAP operating margin 82.3% plus D&A, less some margin give-back as price increases moderate (TrendForce) and opex rises ~$2.5B in FY27.
Peers show only trailing EV/EBITDA (median 13.95x, range 7.0-43.4x), on EBITDA roughly one-third of forward levels. Memory peers at ~4.5x fwd P/E with net cash imply ~3-4x forward EV/EBITDA, so 3.5x.
Net cash $68.3B at 3 Sep 2026 plus about $90-100B of 12-month FCF (FY26 adj. FCF $62.3B; FY27 capex >$50B implied) less higher capital returns from Dec-2026.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Normalized mid-cycle EPS $95 x 12x = $1,140 + ~$60/sh net cash

inputs_detail.derivation: About 45% of FY28 consensus and above FY26's $75.52 non-GAAP EPS. Management says even SCA floor prices give margins 'meaningfully above any prior cycle peak', so mid-cycle earnings are set well above past cycles.
Inside the 11-peer range (3.97-23.73x). Between peak-cycle memory multiples (4-8x) and the less-cyclical storage/controller names (20-24x), which is where memory names trade on normalized earnings.

bear.story: By mid-2027 contract price increases stall. Idaho ID1, Tongluo, CXMT (420k wpm by 2027) and Samsung add bits. The market starts discounting a 2028 price decline (BofA already models a retreat) and a hyperscaler capex pause. MU de-rates to about 4x on falling forward EPS of about $155.

base.story: Supply stays tight through 2027 (SK hynix: 'worst supply year'; TrendForce: HBM supply-constrained, ASP +121%). FY27 EPS lands near $175-185, but price increases moderate. By Oct-2027 investors price FY28 EPS of about $195-205 at a peak-cycle 5.5-6x.

bull.story: HBM resets and the SCA floor structure make the cycle look structurally longer. Shortage runs into 2028 (Micron has 'no line of sight' to balance), and EPS estimates rise toward $250+. The multiple expands to about 7x as the market rewards contracted floors and buybacks from a net cash pile above $150B.

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 3.97x (Macronix) to 23.73x (Seagate). Memory makers cluster at 3.97-8.04x, and storage/controller names at 19.9-23.7x. EV/EBITDA is TRAILING (forward not available from the source): 7.0x (Samsung) to 43.4x (Seagate), median 13.95x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 5.5x NTM P/E is above the 11-peer median (4.92x) and the memory-maker cluster median (about 4.5x), below SNDK's 8.0x, and below MU's own current 6.09x. 3.5x forward EV/EBITDA sits at the low end, consistent with peak-cycle memory valuations. 12x on normalized EPS is inside the full range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: I give a small premium (about 0.6-1.0x P/E) to SK hynix, Samsung and Nanya for three persistent reasons. (1) Contracted revenue: about $150B of RPO at floor prices, plus $32B of customer commitments, mostly cash deposits. That lowers earnings downside versus spot-exposed Taiwan peers. (2) A US listing and capital return without the Korea/Taiwan governance discount that applies to Samsung and SK hynix throughout the horizon. (3) Net cash of $68B. I do not use sell-side outperformance calls. MU stays inside the memory range, not at storage-name multiples, because its earnings are as cyclical as its memory peers'.

thesis_break_reason: $640 is about 40% below the current price and about 3.1x FY28 consensus EPS. At that level the market would most likely be pricing a real turn in the memory cycle, not noise. Signs would be conventional DRAM contract prices flattening or falling in TrendForce data, HBM 2027 resets coming in below expectations, a hyperscaler capex cut, or SCA customers pushing to renegotiate floors. 80% volatility alone rarely takes a stock with $68B net cash and contracted floors that far below fair value.

key_uncertainties: Timing of the memory price peak: TrendForce shows increases decelerating, BofA models a 2028 ASP retreat, and memory stocks have historically peaked before earnings do.
Whether 2027 hyperscaler capex (about $1T+) holds, given financing strain and only modest FCF at the hyperscalers.
Supply response in 2028: Micron, Samsung and SK hynix cleanrooms, plus CXMT at about 550k wpm by end-2028.
How binding SCA floor prices and deposits really are in a downturn.
HBM share against SK hynix and Samsung on HBM4/HBM4E, and GPU makers cutting HBM stack height per device (TrendForce).
Consumer demand destruction: IDC sees the smartphone market's biggest-ever decline in 2026, with only a modest 2027 recovery.
reasoning: Industry evidence is uniformly tight for the next 12 months. TrendForce (29-30 Sep) forecasts 4Q26 conventional DRAM +10-15% QoQ, NAND +15-20%, and 2027 HBM blended ASP +121%. Korea's September chip exports were +263% y/y at $60.3B. SK hynix calls 2027 the worst supply year in industry history. Sandisk and peers are posting 80%+ gross margins. Micron's own FQ4 (rev $54.2B, non-GAAP EPS $33.42) and FQ1 guide ($61.5B, $38.15) confirm this, as do its ~$150B floor-priced RPO and $32B of customer commitments. But the chain also shows the second derivative turning. TrendForce says increases are moderating, BofA models a ~5% 2028 DRAM ASP retreat, consumer units are falling sharply (IDC), and supply arrives from mid-2027 (ID1, Tongluo, CXMT +100k wpm). By Oct-2027 the stock will trade on FY28-29 earnings near a likely cycle peak. Memory peers are priced at 4-8x forward P/E, and MU is already at 6.1x. My three methods give $885-1,200, blended to about $1,064, essentially today's price. I therefore centre the distribution near the current price (median about $1,080 from scenarios: bear $620 at 28%, base $1,100 at 47%, bull $1,800 at 25%). It has a fat left tail for a cycle turn, a right tail for a structurally longer, contract-backed cycle, and an effective volatility of roughly 55-65%, below the trailing 80% that was inflated by a +490% run. Research was limited in two ways: Twelve Data statistics and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan limit / rate limit), and two pages returned 403. Peer multiples come from StockAnalysis, where forward EV/EBITDA is not shown, so trailing figures are reported in that field and labelled.
